accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Geological Society 'Rock cycle' schools pages, BBC Bitesize KS2 'What are rocks?' and the British Geological Survey 'What is soil?' page: soil is a thin layer of weathered rock fragments mixed with organic matter over bedrock; sand grains and pebbles are rock fragments made by weathering and erosion; chalk is a soft sedimentary rock (calcium carbonate). The crust is solid rock under continents and oceans. The lesson deliberately says the outside of Earth is rock, and the adult text notes the hot mantle and liquid outer core so nothing taught has to be unlearned. Breaking boulder to sand is labelled as taking many, many years.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented primary ideas about rocks (Happs 1985 'Children's ideas about rocks'; Dove 1998 review of earth-science misconceptions; Ford 2005): soil goes down forever or Earth is hollow (step 1 predict, challenge tags soil and empty), rocks must be hard so chalk and sand are not rock (step 4 predict, sort feedback for chalk and sand, tag hard), pebbles grow or are made by people (step 3 predict, tags seed and made), and nothing under the sea (step 5 predict, tag air). Tree and cloud decoys in the landscape and a sky decoy in the drill step get their own explanations.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (no flagship lab over 30% similar). 543 How fossils form (flagfoss), 617 Fast and slow Earth changes (flagfastslow) and 560 What is a volcano (flagvolc) never show a soil-to-bedrock cross-section, a boulder breaking into pebbles and sand, or drilling under a city, sea and desert. 286 Hard, soft, rough and smooth sorts by feel, not by whether a thing is rock. The five tasks are specific to the idea that the ground is rock.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each dig reveals one hidden layer (unseen layers stay grey with a ?), so the learner discovers rock under soil before the banner states it. The landscape makes the learner decide place by place, the boulder shows size changing while the material stays rock, the sort forces the soft chalk and tiny sand decisions, and the drill columns generalise to cities, seas and deserts with the sky as a contrast.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the task then disproves: 'Only soil, forever' / 'An empty space' before digging, 'No, sand is like sugar' before finding beach sand, 'They grow from seeds' before breaking the boulder, 'No, rocks are always hard' before the chalk card, and 'Nothing at all' before drilling under the sea. The done message reports whether the prediction was right.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own message: empty (Earth is not hollow), soil (soil is a thin top layer), sugar (sand is rock grains), seed (rocks never grow), hard (chalk is a soft rock), plant, air (under the sea floor is rock), made (water makes pebbles), pebble and mount for the not-rock question. Wrong sorts and wrong taps in the lab also name the slip, e.g. 'Wool comes from a sheep, so it is not rock.'

readability.evidence: Kid text is short sentences with everyday words (validate_lessons readability gate passed: kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Canvas labels are one to three words (Mountain, Beach sand, Dig deeper, Put in: Rock) and banners are one short question. The precise terms boulder, pebbles, solid rock and the adult term bedrock/crust are used where they belong.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (rock under soil; rock you can see; big rocks break small over time; hard or soft still rock and rock all round Earth). The adult text gives curriculum links, the task order and named mistakes with the deep-Earth caveat.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark themes for all six steps (/workspace/shots/r0555rockL2-*, r0555rockD3-*). The canvas sits on its own warm paper panel in dark mode; layer labels, place labels and drill captions fit (drill captions were enlarged to two lines after 'Under a desert' clipped in the first shot); the sort card and both bins are full width; buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Dig deeper, Is it rock? Mountain, Break the rock, Put in: Rock / Not rock, Drill: Under the sea), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with progress, and feedback is spoken with c.say.
